findings.detail: When a quality-tier id is retired, `translateBatch` walks the list and can end up on `gemini-3.1-flash` / `gemini-3-flash-preview` (the last three entries of the quality tier). The only record is `console.warn`. TranslateTab has an `addLog` channel and writes a self-describing banner into the exported workbook precisely because "someone who opens the file months later has no logs and no UI" (components/TranslateTab.tsx:473-475) — yet a catalog translated by Flash instead of Pro is indistinguishable from one translated by Pro in the log, the summary sheet, and the filename. `extractFromMedia` already does the right thing here (geminiService.ts:629, `onProgress?.('Model … unavailable — trying …')`); the translate path is the gap. Trigger is narrow (only after a retirement), which is why this is medium rather than high; it would be high if the degraded model produced a different output schema.
findings.summary: A silent Pro-to-Flash downgrade is recorded only in the browser console

findings.detail: The describe block is introduced as "the highest-consequence behaviour in this change", but `verifyWith` is a hand-written re-implementation of the loop and `verifyGeminiKey` is never imported or called. All four tests would stay green if `verifyGeminiKey` were reverted to a single `resolveModel('fast')` call — the exact regression the block exists to prevent. The docstring is honest about this ("The exact loop `verifyGeminiKey` runs"), which is the tell: the assertion is on the duplicate, so the duplicate is what is protected. The other new suites (`walking the candidate list`, `modelUnavailableError`) do call the real exports and are fine.
findings.summary: The verifyGeminiKey tests exercise a copy of the loop, not verifyGeminiKey

findings.detail: `verifyGeminiKey` deliberately refuses to write to this registry, and the comment at geminiService.ts:129-134 gives the reason: "model availability is per key and per project … striking an id off on its behalf would let testing one key disable a model for another." But every real call path (`translateBatch`, `extractStructuredData`, `processGeneralFile`, `generateText`, `extractFromMedia`) does write to it, keyed on the model id alone — and this app rotates keys (`rotateKey()`, geminiService.ts:211, invoked from the 429 handler at line 311). So if the first key in the textarea lacks access to `gemini-3.1-pro`, that id is struck off for the whole session and the second key — which may well have access — silently gets a weaker model until the page is reloaded. Consequence is degradation, never a hard failure, hence low.
findings.summary: retiredModels is global but availability is per key, contradicting verifyGeminiKey's own rationale

findings.detail: Two leftovers from before `isPartial` was widened past `batchError`. (1) When the run completes but some items came back blank, the Summary sheet reads `Stopped because: N item(s) came back with no translation` (line 493 rendering `partialReason` from line 482) — nothing stopped; every batch ran. (2) The `addLog` at line 520 still asserts unconditionally that "untranslated rows keep their original text", which is the exact inaccuracy the banner immediately above was just fixed to avoid: in `separate` mode the translation column is left blank (lines 494-504, and the write at line 432). A user in `separate` mode reads the log and goes hunting for text that was never written.
findings.summary: Partial-run messaging outside the banner still says "stopped" and "keeps its original text"

findings.detail: The block opens with "Walks the candidate list, exactly as the real calls do" and then, eight lines later, states the opposite: "Walks its OWN copy of the candidate list and never calls `retireModel`" — which is what the code actually does and is the more important fact. The middle paragraph also argues against a version of the function that no longer exists ("Resolving alone was not enough, and the comment that claimed otherwise was wrong"). In a codebase where comments are this load-bearing, a reader who stops at the first line takes away the wrong invariant — and it is the invariant the new test at tests/unit/geminiModels.test.ts:140 exists to protect.
findings.summary: verifyGeminiKey's comment block stacks two contradictory drafts

findings.detail: If every id in `MODEL_CANDIDATES.fast` is unavailable for a key, the loop falls through to `return 'invalid'`. The comment concedes the problem ("a broken app, not a broken key"), but App.tsx:273-275 pipes the result straight into `setGeminiStatus`, so the user sees the same red "invalid" badge and is sent to rotate a key that works — narrower than the bug this PR fixes, but the same failure. `modelUnavailableError`'s useful text is never reached on this path because Test does not call it.
findings.summary: An all-candidates-dead key still reports 'invalid', the misdiagnosis this change set out to fix
